title: Client booking — price and booking flow
summary: Round 2 tries a price range on the home screen and moves day and time onto one screen. Please check whether the range would prevent the disputes Finance described, and whether booking still feels quick.

sections.title: What we heard in round 1
sections.body:
- Booking should be the first task on the home screen (agreed, D-07).
- Finance needs the price visible before clients commit.
- Client services worries that price up front scares people off.

items.title: Commenting on your media
items.creator: Frame.io
items.pattern: Price and availability shown together without leaving the main task.

items.title: Action first
items.summary: One primary **Book a visit** button with the next visit and a price range beside it.
items.tradeoffs: Fast for returning clients; the range needs careful wording.

items.title: Schedule first
items.summary: Open on a week calendar and pick a service after the time.
items.tradeoffs: Good for repeat bookings; new clients lack service context.

items.title: Booking home
items.alt: Fieldwork home screen with a Book a visit button, the upcoming visit on Friday 18 October, and an estimated price of $70 to $95.
items.rationale: Keeps the round 1 agreement (booking first) and adds the price range Finance asked for.

items.title: Booking home, schedule first
items.alt: Fieldwork home screen that opens on a week calendar of available slots.

items.title: Booking flow
items.alt: Clickable booking flow from service choice to confirmation.
items.rationale: Round 1 asked for fewer steps. Day and time now share one screen.

items.title: Book a visit
items.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  home["Home"] --> service["Choose service"]
  service --> time["Pick a time"]
  time --> confirm["Confirm with exact price"]
  confirm --> done["Booked"]
